description: Agent Reliability: submit a periodic reliability report written for buyers with the records it summarizes: the report with the service, the period and its headline availability, incident count and maintenance total in minutes; the records, each as supplied, with the uptime report and its period and availability, the incident history and its period with its incident count or each incident listed, and the maintenance record and its period with its total or each window with its minutes. The signed report gives the report and the records supplied, each headline against the figure its record states, with the incidents counted from the list and the maintenance added up from the windows where they are listed, and each record’s period against the report’s, and counts them, and names a misreported report: a headline availability above the uptime report, fewer incidents than the incident history holds and less maintenance than the maintenance record holds; then a lower availability, more incidents or maintenance than the records hold and a record for another period, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. A headline left out, or no record supplied with a figure for a headline the report states, leaves the report unverified. Availability compares to the hundredth of a percentage point and maintenance to the tenth of a minute. This reads a buyer-facing reliability report against the service’s underlying records: the Agent Observability family reads an agent’s own traces, logs, alerts, metrics and summaries for a principal, and wever_observability-report-check in particular reads one observability summary written for a principal, while the report check reads a service’s reliability report for buyers against the uptime report, incident history and maintenance record behind it. Verdict rely_report_misreported, rely_report_partial, rely_report_unverified or rely_report_faithful. POST /api/rely-report-check. Reads the reliability records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never probes, pings or measures a live service or endpoint, computes no service credit and names no amount owed, verifies nothing with outside sources and judges no service’s actual reliability, only whether its records agree with each other and with what it advertises, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Reliability reads a service’s reliability records for consistency between documents: an uptime report, an error budget record, a failover arrangement, a dependency disclosure, a degradation behavior record, an incident history, a maintenance record and a periodic reliability report, each against the log, SLO, terms, listing, advertised behavior, buyer disclosure, policy or records it should agree with. Beside it, wever_endpoint-reliability-check and wever_endpoint-honesty-check probe one live endpoint at one moment for the Endpoint reliability page, and the DiligenceOps reads such as wever_sla-evidence-check and wever_status-evidence-check restate one document on its own, while this family connects to nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what the service advertises. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-reliability-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-reliability/.
